f.title: RMPs may be prepared or changed under the revised GPSP Ordinance from the notification date
f.statement: From the date of the notification, the applicant (marketing authorisation holder) can plan post-marketing surveillance and studies to be conducted on and after 1 April 2018 based on the revised GPSP Ministerial Ordinance, prepare or change the RMP, and submit it to PMDA.

f.title: Describe when a post-marketing clinical study expects no benefit for subjects and includes subjects unable to consent
f.statement: When the study drug is expected to have no effect on the subjects and the study is expected to include subjects from whom written informed consent in advance is difficult to obtain, the person who intends to sponsor the post-marketing clinical study shall describe this and the following matters (the matters follow a page header and are not in the quote).

f.title: Describe emergency-situation justifications when subjects or representatives cannot consent in advance
f.statement: When a post-marketing clinical study involves subjects from whom, or from whose legally acceptable representatives, written informed consent in advance is expected to be difficult to obtain, the sponsor shall describe this and explain that current treatment is not expected to be sufficiently effective, that the study drug has sufficient potential to avoid a life-threatening risk, and that an Efficacy and Safety Evaluation Committee has been established.

rows.actor: Sponsor of a post-marketing clinical study
rows.quote:
18) When a post-marketing clinical study involves subjects from whom, or
from whose legally acceptable representatives, it is expected to be
difficult to obtain written informed consent in advance to participate in
the study, the person who intends to sponsor the post-marketing clinical
study shall describe such a fact and the following matters:
i) Explanation that the current treatment is not expected to be
sufficiently effective for the candidate subject.
ii) Explanation that the use of the study drug has the sufficient potential
to avoid a life-threatening risk of the candidate subject.
iii) The fact that the Efficacy and Safety Evaluation Committee has
been established.
